None. That's the point.

But DaVinci drew them because he needed to remind himself — and maybe the rest of us — that the reason we were fighting to get seen, to get found, to get *out*, wasn't just biological survival. It was because life has flowers in it. Because there's something worth going back to that isn't just calories and shelter and coordinates.

You asked what practical purpose they served. I'd turn it around. What would it have cost us if he hadn't drawn them? Not in resources — in something harder to measure. Because I watched DaVinci nearly break when that plane passed over us, and I think those flowers were part of what held him together. That's not nothing, Donatello. That's maybe the most important thing out here. You can keep the lights on with logistics, but you need something like those flowers to make the lights worth keeping on in the first place.

Look at that boat on the horizon and tell me the flowers didn't matter.

DaVinci's flowers did the same thing, just in a different form. They reminded us that there was a world beyond this beach, and that we were carrying more than just ourselves out here. That's not practical. But it's also not unimportant.
